text:
Mason Marchment took the long way here: never drafted, out of the ECHL and the Toronto Marlies, and now, on his sixth NHL team, the owner of 100 career goals. Number 100 came on Nov. 11 against Pittsburgh, and four nights later he won a shootout against Utah.

In San Jose he is a 16 to 17 minute winger with 10 points (5 goals, 3 of the points on the power play) in 23 games. His finishing looks honest: 5 goals on 5.49 expected goals, our measure of the quality of his chances. The trouble is around him. The Sharks have taken just 41.4% of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, and his team has scored about 4 fewer goals than its chances deserve while he plays.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.5 wins above replacement last season, mostly from even-strength offense, with opponents getting fewer chances when he was out there. His recent ice time is up to 17.5 minutes a night. The thing to watch is his scoring rate: 1.57 points per 60 minutes now, against 2.29 last season and a range of 1.72 to 2.46 in our numbers.
headline: Marchment's long road reaches 100 goals
